messages:
maya: heads-up — noticed a bunch of small unexpected embedding charges overnight for the background-batcher job :thinking:
maya: they look like partial batches that were retried after a transient reconnect and ended up counted twice
joel: ugh. can you paste the logs?
maya: yea — snippet: ```
2026-02-20T03:21:09Z INFO batcher: start batch id=cb-7e session=svc-async-31 client_req=async_emit seq=12 tokens=0 embeddings=8
2026-02-20T03:21:10Z ERROR uploader: transient network error, retrying batch id=cb-7e
2026-02-20T03:21:11Z INFO router: replayed batch id=cb-7e session=svc-async-31 provisional_charge=8 route=embeddings.background
2026-02-20T03:21:12Z INFO batcher: start batch id=cb-7f session=svc-async-31 seq=13 tokens=0 embeddings=3
2026-02-20T03:21:12Z INFO router: confirmed_charge cb-7e session=svc-async-31 final=true
```
maya: note the provisional_charge log then a confirmed_charge; but our ledger shows both as charged separately
sahil: do we treat provisional charges as separate ledger entries today? i thought provisional was just a transient record and then reconciled away
joel: historically we emit provisional rows to the provisional ledger and then a reconcile job converts them into a single confirmed row. looks like that reconcile didn't match cb-7e -> produced confirmed+left provisional orphan
liz: could be a dedupe key mismatch — the reconcile matches on (session, batch_id) but cb-7e got rehydrated with a new batch_id on replay sometimes (cb-7e -> cb-7e+retry)
noah: i dug into the console telemetry: lots of these come from clients using the async background endpoint with reconnect semantics. they re-submit identical payloads without the original batch_id header, so the router assigns a new batch id and then we end up with provisional+confirmed separate ids
maya: that maps to what I saw in traces. router has two distinct paths: one marks provisional with request.header.x-provisional-id if present, otherwise generates local id. when client drops header on retry, we lose correlation
joel: so two problems: client behavior and server-side reconciliation fragility. which one do we tackle first?
sahil: short-term: make reconcile fuzzy — match by (session, fingerprint(payload), close-enough-timestamp) to collapse. long-term: require and validate a client-supplied id for background batch APIs and document it in SDKs
liz: agree. also we should change the console to surface provisional vs confirmed token counts so support can spot these earlier. currently the dashboard sums everything and hides provisional rows
maya: re UX, propose adding a toggle in the per-route billing view: show provisional rows (yellow badge) and an age column. clicking a row expands raw events (provisional/confirmed)
noah: ops-bot is already generating alerts for provisional > 5m unconfirmed counts, but it doesn't link to customer or session. we should include session id and batch_id in the alert payload
ops-bot: alert created: provisional-orphans/high-count (route=embeddings.background, threshold=100, window=10m)
joel: engineering plan: 1) quick reconcile fuzz-match job (patch) 2) router change to prefer existing provisional_id from payload if present and preserve it across retries 3) server-side validation to reject identical replays without provisional id (non-breaking — warn first) 4) console changes to surface provisional rows + alert link
sahil: for (1) I'll sketch a query: find provisional rows in last 24h where confirmed_count for session and fingerprint is >0 and join on fingerprint to collapse duplicates. need migration to mark collapsed_provisional -> reconciled=true
noah: what about billing implications — do we refund customers for duplicates? finance wants a report
liz: finance: we should auto-credit obvious duplicates for last 72 hours and send an email template. ops: can you synthesize the list?
ops-bot: export requested: provisional-orphans/list -> /internal/exports/prov-orphans-1746001234.csv
maya: i'm going to add two telemetry gauges: provisional_count_by_session and provisional_age_p95. that'll help tune reconcile window
joel: demo of router patch: ```patch
- if (!req.headers.provisional_id) provisional_id = gen();
+ if (req.headers.provisional_id) provisional_id = req.headers.provisional_id; else provisional_id = gen();
```
joel: also add a sticky header propagation in our client SDKs so retries keep the same provisional_id
sahil: will add reconcile job and test in staging. set flag reconcile.fuzzy=true for rollout. measurable success metric: drop orphan_provisional_count by 95% in 24h after patch
liz: for console work I'll mock UI in Figma and add an endpoint to fetch provisional events for a session. PR will include a migration to tag provisional rows with customer_id scoped keys
maya: decision: do quick reconcile + router header handling in one sprint, console and client SDK docs next sprint. ops to run export and credit affected customers after engineering sign-off
noah: noted. can we add a small e2e to simulate reconnect-without-header and ensure ledger dedupe? otherwise this will regress
sahil: yep i'll add a test harness that simulates async client retries with/without provisional header and asserts single confirmed row
maya: thanks team. I'll file the follow-ups: https://redwood/issue/PLAT-embed-provisional-1746001234 and assign tasks
joel: thanks — patch review in the afternoon. :thumbsup:
meter-bot: metric emit: provisional_orphans_count=137 host=router-3 route=embeddings.background
maya: closing for now. we'll update this thread with patch links and charge reconciliation results
